text:
Anna R: quick spike idea — propose a compact "claim-checkpoint" onboarding flow for Private control plane (aim: <30s happy-path, minimal net egress, auditable handoff). want quick feedback before i write an RFC :thinking:
Mike L: sounds promising. high level? how is it different from our current peering + cert bootstrap?
Anna R: current flows assume long-lived peering or heavy operator steps. this is ephemeral-claim-first: customer agent requests a one-time claim token from control plane, exchanges over PrivateLink/endpoint, then receives a short-lived signed cert + tenant routing claim. no peering changes needed for most customers.
Julio P: wait — so no peering means we avoid VPC attachments for initial onboard. but what's the trust anchor? where do we validate the customer?
Anna R: trust anchors: 1) customer provides a pre-authorized onboarding token (from console or partner API) OR 2) we verify an outbound-initiated mTLS handshake where agent proves possession of customer KMS-signed nonce. control plane issues a signed tenant cert valid for N minutes.
SRE Bot: note: ephemeral certs mean fewer long-lived routes to manage. consider metrics: issue_rate, accept_rate, token_failures, cert_rotate_failures. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Sarah K: product: how will this look to customers? need clear UX: "Create claim" -> agent runs CLI -> success. also TTLs and renewal UX. can we auto-rotate for Dedicated customers?
Anna R: yes — UX: in Console -> Onboarding -> Create claim (scoped to project) -> copy claim URL or use API. Example minimal exchange (agent -> control plane):
```json
POST /v1/onboard/claims
{
  "claim_id": "CLAIM-abc123",
  "agent_nonce": "base64nonce",
  "local_vpc": "10.10.0.0/16",
  "desired_interfaces": ["private-endpoint"],
  "metadata": {"env":"prod"}
}
```
Anna R: control plane responds with a signed payload: cert (PEM), route assertion blob (signed), and a short-lived relay token. Agent uses that cert to open the first authenticated control plane connection and to present the route assertion to edge when creating endpoint resources.
Mike L: what about replay? do we bind claim to the agent's ephemeral key and to the IP? also need a one-time-use constraint.
Anna R: claim is single-use, state transitions: CREATED -> CONSUMED -> ACTIVE. signed assertion includes agent_pubkey_fingerprint + claim_nonce. if consumed, the claim cannot be reused. we also require outbound connection from agent to control plane within a 2 minute window after claim creation unless customer sets longer TTL.
Julio P: network-wise, does this require any NAT or special ENI? or can it reuse existing private endpoint patterns?
Anna R: reuse PrivateLink where available; fallback to regional relay for older accounts. no ENI-level changes. for Dedicated customers we can optionally create per-tenant ENIs later as a separate step after the claim is ACTIVE.
SRE Bot: ops note: we should cap concurrent claims per account to avoid abuse and rate-limit per-IP. also track lifecycle metrics for billing + incident triage.
Sarah K: product question: can we make claims multi-tenant (multiple agents consume a single claim)?
Anna R: by default single-consumer. we can support a "team-claim" mode where a claim issues a CA-signed intermediate, but that has bigger blast radius — that would be explicit opt-in for enterprise.
Ben (product): also add audit fields to the console: created_by, consumed_by, consumed_from_ip, consumed_at. customers (security teams) want that for SOC2.
Mike L: failure modes? agent gets cert but then fails to attach route — we need rollback and TTL expiry flows, plus a quick-revoke API.
Anna R: yes: control plane keeps a short-lived state and exposes revoke endpoint. route assertions have embedded expiry; edge checks expiry before accepting traffic. if agent fails to establish downstream endpoints within X minutes, we garbage-collect resources and mark claim FAILED.
Julio P: curious about egress cost: if many customers use regional-relay fallback we'll spin up more relay capacity. we should simulate expected RPS and cost delta.
Anna R: agreed — next action: i'll run a small traffic model for 3 scenarios (1000 onboard/day; 10k/day; 50k/day) and estimate relay instance-hours and avg latency impact.
Sarah K: timeline? if we like spike outcome, can we fold into onboarding RFC for next sprint?
Anna R: i can do spike + costing + short RFC draft this week. anyone want to pair on threat model?
Julio P: i'll help with threat model and replay/nonce validation details.
Mike L: i'll look at edge checks and GC windows.
Ben (product): i'll write user-facing flow and audit requirements.
Anna R: awesome — i'll post the spike results here when done. thanks all :thumbsup:
SRE Bot: deploy-bot: created ticket INFRA-1345 for relay capacity estimation.
